author: Anshul Verma
content:
[🤖 Claude Code] Adopted. Action: comments become a separate, clearly documented channel:

- Docs: the skill gets its own reference page for actions, and every gated doc plus the tracker carries a short "How to steer this run" box listing the comment kinds side by side (question, answer to Qn, requirement, Action:, Approved, Changes:) with one example each.
- Handling: an Action: is acknowledged at once with "Running: <the action restated>", executed in the main loop (never by a subagent), and closed with an outcome reply. Anything destructive or outward-facing waits for your "Confirm" reply in the same thread.
- Visibility: actions get their own table on the tracker (time, action, status, outcome) and a distinct entry in the event log.

author: Anshul Verma
content: In addition to the tracker doc I want a global doc (private) that tracks my own velocity depending on the complexity of the doc I am reviewing. It should account for time I am spending reading actively only. I also want to see a complexity score and estimate time for reading metrics for every doc
quoted_text: A live tracker doc shows what the skill is doing and what it is waiting on.

author: Anshul Verma
content: [🤖 Claude Code] Adopted, and added to the doc as open question 8 (how to measure active reading). Plan: one private "Review velocity" doc shared across all runs. Every gated doc gets a complexity score (words, figures, open questions, reading grade, unfamiliar terms) and an estimated reading time from your own measured pace. Google Docs exposes no "viewed" events, only comments and edits, so active reading time has to be inferred from your comment bursts. We recommend counting a reading session from first to last comment with gaps under 10 minutes, plus a fixed lead-in per session, and calibrating the lead-in against the estimates over time.

type: proposal

purpose: get the design of the galley skill accepted, with its seven open questions answered or left to their recommendations, before the skill is built

author: Anshul Verma (first person plural)

readers: Anshul, the decision-maker and the only user; knows sdd, marginalia, humanize and the ShopEV run; answers each open question by commenting on it

destination: private Google Doc; acceptance is a comment on the title

length: 2 pages of body

depth: decision

targets: default

max_passes: 3

ask: answer the open questions by commenting on them, then accept by commenting "Approved" on the title; owner Anshul Verma

tone: direct, engineer to engineer

keep: the seven numbered open questions with recommendation and default; no Nomenclature appendix (the reader knows the identifiers)

avoid: naming people as the source of runs, diffs or docs

confirmed: no (guessed; requirements from the user's request on 2026-10-18)

author: Anshul Verma
content: I want the skill to reflect that its main purpose is to automate development workflow in a structured manner. It will produce bunch of proposals, review them with me one by one and build using proper development strategy. Give me more options
quoted_text: What should the skill be called? We recommend galley, after the galley proofs an author marks up in the margins and signs off before printing. Alternatives are margin-call and say-so. If unanswered: galley.

author: Anshul Verma
content:
[🤖 Claude Code] More options, aimed at "structured development workflow, reviewed with you one doc at a time":

- lockstep (recommended): you and the skill move together, one reviewed doc at a time, then build in order.
- ratchet: every accepted doc locks progress in; work only moves forward.
- foreman: runs the build site, checks every plan with the owner first.
- shipwright: builds methodically, plank by plank, to a drawn plan.
- waypoint: each doc is a waypoint you sign off before the next leg.
- keel: lays the structural backbone first, then builds on it.

galley is still on the table. Q1 stays open until you pick one.
